title: Stranded as war nears: Paris, Jimmy Monroe, the night train
summary: With Bobby gone, Ramirez found Americans were being repatriated via Paris, met Jimmy Monroe, and escaped by night train through Belgium to Rotterdam.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Was a single. And "Watching Your Money Dwindle."
Bass and I, we were looking for the next boat to go home.

Bass said...I don't know how... Bass decided to go one way or the other; I don't remember just how. He went...I don't know, he went somewhere, and I was left alone. So how I heard... The consul told me that there was an organization that was taking Americans back home, but you had to go to Paris. But in order to go to Paris you had to go through Belgium, with a night train. Relations must have strained at the time, because they were (?) on the alert -- because there was always blackouts and...
Well, it must have been the war then.

Yeah. So I went and took that train. I got to Paris. I went through Belgium and we stopped at different places all through the night, you know. I got through, I got to Rotterdam, and I was immediately taken by the police, you know; they want you to show identification and all of that...

Oh, first of all... I got to Paris first. Before I left out of Paris, Billie Holiday's ex-husband, Jimmy Monroe, was there. I met him. And the streets were clean, just like... I don't know Casablanca ever got that atmosphere (?)about Paris, getting out of Paris, but that was... For me, that was like a background! It was clean, the streets were... People were leaving the city. It wasn't the Paris that I knew. I hung out with Jimmy Monroe, and we went to the consulate, where... Well, he helped me leave; you know, negotiated to get this ticket and paid it, and I would pay when I got home, you know.

So one night we took the train, quietly, out of the Gare St. Lazare. I remember the night ride all through, going through... I didn't know if a bomb was coming or not! But anyhow, the next day we arrived. I wouldn't get off the train to see old friends or anything, because this was my last chance -- I wanted to get the hell out!

I got to Rotterdam, met some girlfriend, acquaintances that I had there. They were very nice to me and helped me. We talked about old times, etcetera, and what happened to this one and what happened to that one, you know. And that's how I got home.
